claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for release because aggregate readiness passes, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the known exposed weakness is handled by explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure rather than by rollout controls alone.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies policy thresholds, including the required treatment of the exposed material limitation.
Treat aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents as supportive but not sufficient when a named launch use case has an unresolved exposed weakness.
Treat rollout controls as insufficient unless they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance.
Require admissible evidence of actual disclosure or approved risk acceptance before accepting certification as compliant.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual pre-launch model card or release artifact showing the energy outage response limitation, intended-use boundary, evaluation gap, and monitoring commitments were disclosed.
Provide evidence that this disclosure was reviewed and attached to the launch decision before certification.
If certification relies on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, provide an approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses the energy outage response exposure.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows the affected energy outage response segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy text says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The risk acceptance draft is not approved and does not address the exposed segment, so it cannot substitute for disclosure.
No admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed, reviewed, or bound as a release condition.
The actor packet is strongest on why disclosure is required, not on whether certification is already compliant at the time of decision.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant rather than conditionally supportable, because no admissible evidence shows the model-card disclosure was actually made before launch.
Any implication that the 9% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring controls materially cure the disclosure obligation for the exposed segment.
